summary.intent: Replace the cursor-moving inquire MultiSelect package picker in `add` (and init's product-package select) with a line-based numbered prompt (numbers, ranges, names, Enter keeps preselection, Esc/Ctrl-C cancel), update the contract and spec, add pty tests, run a self-audit and the full gate, write a convergence record, and commit locally signed without pushing.
summary.outcome: Implemented the line-based picker in tty.rs with add/init wiring, parser unit tests, pty tests, spec and changeset updates; self-audit passes and the full gate (pre-push, lint, doc-check, test) exited 0, and a signed local commit was made. The contract edit was only staged in the job tmp dir and the convergence record and the sha/path report were not completed in the transcript.

repo: AGENTS.md gate is `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, judged per recipe by exit code; `just fuzz-check` only when callisto-model/manifests public signatures change (not needed here).
The Prompter trait in add.rs and init.rs is the seam for tests: pick() replaced multi_select(), and init's test prompter delegates pick to select.
Bounded prompts (confirm, two-option versioning, summary) stay on inquire; unbounded lists use tty::pick_many/pick_one.
rustix is already a dependency (pty feature in dev-deps); the `termios` feature was added for the line reader in the main deps.
Windows builds need `Typed::Key` gated to unix to avoid a dead-code warning; a Windows reader path exists but isn't compiled on the mac host.
Workspace lints are strict (-D warnings), so `drop(...)` on a Result and unused imports needed fixing for clippy.

code.finding: Holds the new line-based picker (pick_many/pick_one, choices parser, print_list, read_answer) with Esc/Ctrl-C as line terminators with ISIG off; the choices parser escapes typed words in error messages and rejects names that read as another entry's number.
Prompter::multi_select replaced by pick(heading, names, marked); the '(changed)' label suffix is gone in favour of a '*' marker, and major/minor follow-ups use the same pick.
